activity.notes: Athanagild's widow Goiswintha is independently documented through her subsequent remarriage to Liuvigild. As scholarship states that the date of her original marriage to Athanagild is NOT established, 567 is a SOURCE-ANCHORED REPRESENTATIVE POINT for the end of that relationship at Athanagild's death, not a claim that the entire consortship lasted one year or started in 554. Do not synthesize a 554–567 personal rail from Athanagild's royal reign alone.

sources.title: María Rosario Valverde Castro (2008), Mujeres «viriles» en la Hispania visigoda. Los casos de Gosvinta y Benedicta, Studia Historica. Historia Medieval 26, pp.17–44
sources.citation_text: Researches Gosvinta's political agency and explicitly cautions that although the marriage to Athanagild is attested, the wedding's precise date is unknown.

sources.title: Ana María Jiménez Garnica (2008), Gosuintha, el fracaso de una coniux real, Studia Historica. Historia Antigua 26
sources.citation_text: University of Salamanca focused study of queen Gosuintha's marital and royal political position under Athanagild, Liuvigild, and the subsequent royal court; interpret court claims critically.

sources.title: Deutsche Biographie — Godiswintha, Westgothenkönigin
sources.citation_text: Biographical reference identifies the queen as Athanagild's wife, her later marriage to Leovigild, and her activity/death under Reccared; traditional dating of 554 for the first consort period is not a proved wedding date.
